script.base: A 3-point, 43-total game (PIT 23 / NO 20) stays competitive, not a blowout. Pittsburgh leans on Jaylen Warren, who has 46 carries for 244 yards and 16 targets for 148 yards over weeks 4-6, into a Saints run defense allowing 5.07 YPC and 21 runs of 10+. NO blitzes 35% and Rodgers' EPA/dropback is -0.34 vs blitz versus -0.04 unblitzed, so the pass game tilts short (Germie Bernard 23 targets, 84 air yards; Warren -15 air) rather than a pure DK Metcalf shot script (28 targets, 288 air). New Orleans, only +3, keeps Kendre Miller as the lead back (36/109, 3.0 YPC) with Alvin Kamara (17/69 rush, 13 targets/64 rec) and Chris Olave (25 targets, 310 air) as the throw outlets against a tighter Steelers run defense (4.19 YPC).
script.flip1: The 35% NO blitz gets home, Pittsburgh falls behind, and the ball leaves Warren's carries for Metcalf deep shots. That is the Warren rush+rec under path: weeks 4-6 already contain a 78 rush+rec game (listed last4 176, 126, 188, 78; the 176 reconciles as the game outside this window, so the in-window set is 126, 188, 78).
script.flip2: Pittsburgh leads late and clocks it with Warren, while New Orleans abandons the run. Miller's carries die and Tyler Shough (6 rush, 38 yards in three weeks) plus Olave/Devaughn Vele throw to catch up. A 3-point spread limits true blowout benching, so Warren's snaps are safer than in a 10-point script.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and Warren under 96.5 lost the ticket. The 78-yard game was the template, not the outlier: New Orleans put extra bodies in the box on the only back who matters, Shepherd played, and Dowdle's knee was fine enough to take 8-10 carries. Rodgers at -0.34 EPA versus a 35% blitz took sacks instead of the -15-air checkdowns, and the few completions went to Bernard (23 targets) and Metcalf. A regressed day — about 12 carries at 4.0 YPC (48) plus 25 receiving — lands near 73, and the market's 50/50 price at 96.5 was the sharp regression, not a stale line. That counter is real, which is why this is flagged rather than sized as a lock, but it is not stronger than the base read: the front still allows 5.07 YPC and 21 runs of 10+, and two of the three in-window games cleared 96.5 by 30 and 92.
slip_story: Single-script stack: Pittsburgh modest lead, run the soft NO front, check down when blitzed. Warren rush+rec over 96.5 is the only leg. Do not add a total over (43 is modest, weather unknown), a Metcalf over (blitz split fights it), or a Miller under (the 70 is inside weeks 4-6). A later Dowdle inactive would strengthen this same story; it does not create a second market.
